$doc: Vyomi capability registry — GCP Memorystore for Redis. See aws/s3.json for the contract. Feature ids share one namespace with the AWS registry, so they are prefixed gcp.memorystore.*

gcp.memorystore.instances.title: Instances (create, list, get, patch, delete)
limitations: Instances are READY immediately; Vyomi has no provisioning delay (CREATING) to model.

gcp.memorystore.failover.title: Failover (Standard tier)
limitations: Failover swaps the current/alternative zone instantly; Vyomi has no replication lag or brief unavailability window to model.

gcp.memorystore.import-export.title: Import / export (Cloud Storage RDB)
limitations: Vyomi validates the gs:// destination/source shape and returns a completed operation, but does not read or write an actual RDB file in Cloud Storage — the data plane content is unchanged by import/export.

gcp.memorystore.maintenance.title: Maintenance window and reschedule
limitations: Vyomi never runs maintenance in the background; rescheduleMaintenance only records the requested schedule on the instance.

gcp.memorystore.connections.title: Connections (endpoint, AUTH string, in-transit encryption)
limitations: The host:port shown is a real Redis-protocol endpoint only when the appliance's shared Valkey data plane is configured (offline); otherwise (Nano, no data plane) it is a deterministic address and the console says so.
serverCaCerts are synthetic placeholders — Vyomi does not run a real TLS CA, so a client cannot actually negotiate TLS against the returned certificate.

gcp.memorystore.read-replicas.title: Read replicas (replica count, read endpoint)
limitations: Read replicas are modeled as a replica count and a read endpoint on the SAME instance (matching the control-plane shape of Instance.readReplicasMode/replicaCount); Vyomi does not run separate replica processes, so the read endpoint serves the same data plane as the primary endpoint.

gcp.memorystore.nodes.title: Nodes
limitations: Node ids and the primary/replica role are derived client-side from the instance's tier and node count, not a dedicated API field (the native NodeInfo message only carries id and zone); there is no per-node telemetry (CPU, memory, connections) behind them.

gcp.memorystore.monitoring.title: Overview: Monitoring (memory usage, connected clients)
limitations: Vyomi collects no Redis runtime metrics (memory usage, connected clients, ops/sec) for Memorystore instances.
